summary: Session-affinity 'blink' during canary switchover causes routed requests to degraded variant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a brief loss of session-affinity ('blink') for a subset of user sessions during an automated canary rollback window. Affected requests were rerouted to a cost-optimized variant (redwood/safe-v1.0) instead of the pinned model (redwood/open-v1.3-quant), resulting in degraded output quality and an unexpected token billing increase.

Impact:
- ~3% of BrightMaps' traffic in us-east observed mixed-model responses for 12 minutes.
- Customer reported quality regression in end-user-facing scoring and a spike in per-token cost due to repeated retries.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (BrightMaps reserved cluster #bm-legacy-2) in us-east.
- Traffic pattern: steady 750 r/s with 98th pct sequence length ~120 tokens.

Relevant timestamps: 2026-03-10 18:04:12 UTC (first anomaly) — 2026-03-10 18:16:30 UTC (resolved via hotfix).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a tenant with an explicit model_pin to redwood/open-v1.3-quant on a dedicated cluster.
2) Start steady traffic representative of BrightMaps workload (long-tail sequences).
3) Trigger a canary rollback by toggling canary weight from 10% to 0% while orchestrator prewarm jobs are in flight.
4) Observe session-affinity markers and routing decisions at edge and orchestrator during the 1st 30s of the rollback.
Expected: pinned sessions remain bound to the pinned model for the lease window; fallback only for health failures.
Observed: transient rebind to safe variant and a small cohort of sessions sent to the degraded model for multiple requests.
logs:
Edge traces: trace-id=01-7f2ab3-9c4d2a; sample-req-id=bm-req-3c9f; error: none (successful 200s but wrong model).
Orchestrator: prewarm-mirror write at 2026-03-10T18:04:09Z overwrote lease metadata for cohort bm-tenant-42 (write-actor=prewarm-mirror, precedence=high).
Serving logs: variant-selection=redirect -> variant=safe-v1.0 reason=prewarm-fallback.
Billing telemetry: 18:05-18:15 token spike +24% vs baseline.
Attached artifacts: s3://redwood-support/SUP-451999/edge-traces.log, s3://redwood-support/SUP-451999/orch-dump.json
comments: 2026-03-10 18:22 - Aisha Kline (Support): Initial triage completed; reproducer requested and cluster diagnostics collected. Asking SRE to check prewarm mirror precedence and lease mutation ordering.

2026-03-10 18:40 - Marcus Chen (SRE): Found that prewarm-mirror write occurred with unexpected high precedence during rollback. Hypothesis: prewarm mirror had higher precedence than existing session lease due to earlier change in precedence matrix (PR ref provided). Will test reverting precedence in staging.
2026-03-10 19:05 - BrightMaps (Customer - Tanya Rao): Confirmed users seeing lower-quality outputs and some retries; provided example request ids bm-req-3c9f, bm-req-3d11.

2026-03-10 20:10 - Elena Martinez (Eng): Deployed a hotfix to lower prewarm-mirror precedence and added a guard that prevents lease overwrite if session-lease.is_active == true. Monitoring metrics now show rebind rate dropping to baseline.

2026-03-11 09:12 - Aisha Kline (Support): Followed up with customer; BrightMaps reports restored quality and acceptable billing delta after remediation. Closing incident with follow-up actions listed.

2026-03-12 15:03 - Elena Martinez (Eng): Postmortem draft posted to Confluence; change scheduled to make precedence explicit in orchestrator config and add unit tests covering rollback+prewarm interactions. See linked PR.
investigation_notes: Prewarm-mirror writes were introduced to reduce cold-start latency during canary windows; default precedence was inadvertently set higher than session-lease revision in a recent change (orchestrator PR #4599).
Session-lease TTLs were normal; the issue is lease metadata mutation order rather than expiry. Edge accepted routing decision based on newest metadata even when it originated from prewarm actor.
Affected cohort size small (~3% of traffic) because only sessions with concurrent prewarm writes and in-flight requests saw overwritten lease state.
No 5xx or auth failures observed — purely routing metadata inconsistency.
resolution:
Hotfix applied 2026-03-10 19:02 UTC: revert prewarm-mirror precedence to previous level and add an atomic compare-and-set on session-lease to prevent active-lease overwrites. Canary rollback drain policy updated to serialize prewarm completions before committing weight=0.
Customer communication: sent incident summary, examples of affected request ids, and recommended client-side retries backoff to BrightMaps.
Follow-ups: engineering to land PR #4678 (orch precedence fixes) and add e2e test covering rollback+prewarm. Postmortem published: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/SUP-451999+Postmortem
follow_up_actions: Ship PR #4678 to orchestrator to make prewarm precedence explicit and covered by unit tests.
Add an observability alert for 'session-lease-rebind-rate' > 0.5% sustained over 5m during canary windows.
Update canary runbook to require serialization of prewarm mirror completes before weight zero commit.
Coordinate a scheduled maintenance window to roll the precedence change across dedicated clusters to avoid transient drift.
